newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico begins battle against ergot sorghum fungus.
newsitem.headline: Mexico begins battle against ergot sorghum fungus.

text.p: Mexico declared a national emergency in its fight to prevent the spread of ergot fungus that has afflicted at least ten sorghum producing regions, the Agriculture Ministry said on Monday.
The emergency measures call for 90 days of regulated treatments and harvesting, the ministry said in a document obtained by Reuters.
As part of the precautions, seed produced in areas known to be contaminated cannot be planted in other regions and all sorghum seed must be analyzed and tested, the ministry said.

It listed the ten regions in three states where the fungus has been discovered as Mante, Altamira, Xicotencatl, Gonzalez and San Fernando in Tamaulipas state; Ebano, Tamuin and San Vicente de Tancuayala in San Luis Potosi state; and Panuco in Veracruz state.

Mexican Seed Association spokesman Manuel Galvan Izquierdo told Reuters the regions are not the most major sorghum producing regions, but are located near more important regions. Top sorghum growing states are Guanajuato, Tamaulipas and San Luis Potosi, he added.
"Ergot eats the sorghum seed before it is fertilized," Galvan said.

He said the fungus' presence was discovered in Mexico a month and a half ago. In 1995 the disease cost Brazil $3 million in lost sorghum crops, Galvan added, and has also afflicted crops in Puerto Rico and may have struck Texas.

The association has organized a conference in Matamoros, Tamaulipas state, on April 15, with presentations by Bayer and other companies on chemicals to combat the fungus. Galvan said the chemicals are not guaranteed to eradicate ergot.
